title: India's cultural and leisure time is widespread, but gendered unpaid work changes who can actually use it
source_unit: National Statistics Office India Time Use Survey 2024
geography: India; persons aged 6 years and above, with national, gender, age, and rural-urban estimates

denominator.unit: surveyed persons aged 6 years and above; 228,576 male and 225,565 female respondents

culture_leisure_media_sports_participati.unit: percent participating in culture, leisure, mass-media, or sports activities during the reference day

culture_leisure_media_sports_time_per_pa.unit: minutes per day among participants in culture, leisure, mass-media, or sports activities

culture_leisure_media_sports_time_per_pe.unit: minutes per day averaged across all persons aged 6 years and above

mechanism.value: Cultural, leisure, media, and sports time is nearly universal as a daily category, but the available duration still competes with work, care, learning, and self-maintenance

observations.method: India TUS 2024 diary-style time-use collection in 30-minute slots, coding activities under ICATUS 2016; estimates distinguish participation rate, time per participant, and time per person.
observations.uncertainty: The category combines culture, leisure, mass media, and sports, so it cannot be interpreted as formal cultural participation or a single consumer activity; the one-day reference period does not establish habitual or seasonal behavior.
observations.subgroup: Persons aged 6 years and above represented by the national TUS sample; age, sex, and rural-urban breakdowns are available in the fact sheet.
observations.counterinterpretation: High participation may reflect brief or passive media use, while lower time per person may reflect nonparticipation or multiple simultaneous activities; the category is intentionally broad.

denominator.unit: surveyed persons aged 6 years and above; gender-specific estimates are based on the reported male and female respondent counts

female_unpaid_domestic_participation.unit: percent of females participating in unpaid domestic services for household members during the reference day

male_unpaid_domestic_participation.unit: percent of males participating in unpaid domestic services for household members during the reference day

female_domestic_time_per_participant.unit: minutes per day among female participants in unpaid domestic services

male_domestic_time_per_participant.unit: minutes per day among male participants in unpaid domestic services

female_care_time_per_participant.unit: minutes per day among female participants in unpaid caregiving

male_care_time_per_participant.unit: minutes per day among male participants in unpaid caregiving

culture_time_female_vs_male.value: 164 versus 177 minutes per day among female versus male participants in culture, leisure, mass media, and sports

mechanism.value: The same survey category shows near-universal leisure participation while unpaid domestic and care work is strongly gendered, making cultural time an unequal conversion resource rather than a neutral preference

observations.method: India TUS 2024 gender estimates using the same 24-hour diary framework; durations are per participant, not per entire population.
observations.uncertainty: The estimates are descriptive and do not identify bargaining, household structure, simultaneous activities, income, employment quality, or whether reduced cultural time is caused by unpaid work.
observations.subgroup: Male and female participants aged 6 years and above; the fact sheet includes transgender persons in the person category but does not provide a separate duration estimate here.
observations.counterinterpretation: Different participation rates and activity reporting may reflect age composition, social norms, or measurement conventions; culture/leisure/media/sports includes activities with different degrees of agency and social value.

denominator.unit: surveyed persons aged 6 years and above; rural and urban estimates are reported by sector

rural_culture_leisure_media_sports_parti.unit: percent of rural persons participating in culture, leisure, mass-media, or sports activities

urban_culture_leisure_media_sports_parti.unit: percent of urban persons participating in culture, leisure, mass-media, or sports activities

rural_culture_time_per_participant.unit: minutes per day among rural participants

urban_culture_time_per_participant.unit: minutes per day among urban participants

age_6_14_culture_time_per_person.unit: minutes per day among persons aged 6-14, averaged across all persons in the group

age_15_59_culture_time_per_person.unit: minutes per day among persons aged 15-59, averaged across all persons in the group

mechanism.value: Urban residence is associated with slightly broader and longer culture/leisure/media/sports time, while children have substantially more daily time in the broad category than working-age adults

observations.method: India TUS 2024 rural-urban and age-group estimates using the same 24-hour activity diary and ICATUS classification.
observations.uncertainty: These comparisons do not identify venue supply, commuting, household income, school schedules, digital access, or causal effects of urban residence and age.
observations.subgroup: Rural versus urban persons, and persons aged 6-14 versus 15-59 years.
observations.counterinterpretation: The higher child time may reflect school-age media and play categories, while adult time may be shifted into work, care, or socializing that is not coded as culture; urban differences are modest relative to within-household gender differences.

related_sources.claim: Full Time Use in India 2024 report provides the detailed tables and methodology behind the factsheet.
Official factsheet documents the survey sample, diary reference period, ICATUS classification, participation rates, and time durations.

boundary: This record adds observed time-allocation evidence linking cultural/leisure/media time to unpaid domestic work, caregiving, gender, age, and rural-urban context. The category is broad and combines culture, leisure, mass media, and sports; the one-day diary does not establish habitual cultural consumption, quality, preference, or causality.
